text:
pagerbot: PAGER: edge-auth anomaly detected — severity P1. High volume of 401/403s from a small IP set; possible header scraping and suspicious log drain activity. Paging oncall. Playbook: https://redwood.playbooks/incidents/auth-exfil

ryan: oncall-ryan here, acknowledging. I'll gather initial telemetry and coordinate.

maya: seeing a sharp spike from proxy node edge-45. ~2k 401s/min, source IPs 34.87.23.90 and 34.87.23.91. Many requests include truncated Authorization headers in proxy debug logs.

ev an: can we confirm any *complete* tokens in logs? quick grep across last 3 hours?

maya: quick grep results: ~12 header fragments that look like `Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGci...` (truncated). Found entries landed in staging bucket path `s3://staging-logs/proxy/2026/03/18/edge-45/part-0003.gz` — currently internal. No confirmed full tokens yet but fragments include long base64-like strings.

ryan: blocking the source IPs at edge ACLs now. Applying temporary denylist and routing to sinkhole.

 t ess: running firewall call — pushing block for both IPs:

```
curl -X POST "https://edge-firewall.internal/api/v1/blocks" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $EDGE_API_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"ip":"34.87.23.90","reason":"suspicious-auth-scrape"}'
```

 t ess: blocked 34.87.23.90 and 34.87.23.91. edge-45 showing drop in incoming connections from those IPs.

evan: I'm running a search for full token patterns across all recent buckets and forwarding pipelines. If we find any, we'll rotate and revoke immediately.

maya: also found a suspicious external drain target in the forwarder config: `https://logs.example-cdn.net/ingest` — looks like an indexing job had an unexpected push after 02:12 UTC. That forwarder is svc-log-forwarder.

ryan: immediate action items (short):
1) Block IPs (done)
2) Suspend the `svc-log-forwarder` job (maya/tess)
3) Snapshot and preserve evidence of affected logs (evan)
4) Rotate any service keys that may have been used by the forwarder (ryan/tess)
5) Legal & security notified for customer-impact assessment (ryan -> legal)

legal: looped in. We need counts of exposed entries, whether tokens are complete, and which customers' tenant IDs appear in the artifacts. Please preserve full buckets and avoid deleting.

maya: suspended the forwarder job in staging and prod (job id `logfwd-77a`). Confirmed the drain endpoint unreachable now.

evan: search finished: found 3 artifacts that contain what appear to be *full* Authorization headers (masked below). Marked as evidence and copied to secure forensics bucket (read-only): `s3://forensics/evidence/2223334444/`

Found (masked):
- `Authorization: Bearer eyJ***X9aT`
- `Authorization: Bearer eyJ***kLmN`
- `Authorization: Bearer eyJ***qP0z`

All three are truncated in logs ingestion but forensic copy shows full token strings prior to ingestion.

ryan: rotating service keys for `svc-log-forwarder` and issuing revocations for tokens that match those patterns. Executing revoke script now.

```
./scripts/rotate_service_key.sh svc-log-forwarder --force --notify=security
```

 t ess: rotation script completed, new key provisioned. Old keys disabled. Confirming that forwarder no longer authenticates outbound.

sre-oncall: starting broader scope check — searching for any other outlier drains or abnormal egress in telemetry (netflow + egress buckets). ETA ~20m.

maya: snapshot of staging bucket taken and moved to `s3://forensics/snapshots/2223334444/`. ACLs tightened (access limited to sec/forensics/legal).

legal: thanks. We'll triage customer notification requirements after sec assesses which tenant IDs are affected. Keep evidence retention on. No public statements until we confirm scope.

ryan: security, please confirm whether these tokens were used to call any write APIs after exfil timeframe. If yes, consider forced session revocation for affected tenants.

evan: cross-checking token use in access logs. So far, two of the three tokens show activity post-ingest: one used to call `POST /v1/infer` from a suspicious IP 203.0.113.47 at 02:20 UTC. Flagging for immediate session invalidation.

ryan: invalidated sessions for the affected tokens and rolled short-term mitigations for the tenants. Created ticket: IID-2026-86 (auth-exfil).

maya: quick customer-impact note: three tenants affected, appears limited to staging staging-svc and one customer sandbox. No production tenant keys found so far.

legal: request to preserve communication logs with the three tenants in case we need to reach out. Also prepare incident notification draft but hold until sec confirms.

sre-oncall: monitoring in place. Edge traffic back to baseline after blocklist and drain suspension. We'll keep elevated watch for 4 hours and then hand to postmortem.

ryan: summary update: mitigations executed (blocks, forwarder suspended, keys rotated, evidence preserved, sessions invalidated). Security and legal engaged. Preparing customer notification plan pending final scope.

pagerbot: INCIDENT UPDATE: Mitigations applied and monitoring active. Transitioning to postmortem channel #postmortems/2223334444 in 4h unless further escalation.

maya: adding a single immediate mitigation note — add stricter scrubbing at proxy level to never log Authorization beyond first 8 chars. Raising a config PR now.

ryan: thanks team. Stand down for now but remain available.
